To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
privacy and utility are two different concepts, and that the privacy- utility tradeoff in data anonymization is similar to the well-known risk-return tradeoff for financial investment.

(1) Privacy and utility are fundamentally different, and should not be compared directly; (2) The privacy-utility trade-off in data publishing is fundamentally similar to the risk-reward trade-off in financial investment; (3) We propose an integrated framework to consider the privacy-utility (risk-reward) trade-off, borrowing concepts from Modern Portfolio Theory; (4) We evaluate our methodology on a real dataset, and show that the privacy- and utility-related misconceptions in data publishing are

(a) the tradeoff between data privacy and utility is similar to the tradeoff between risk and return in financial investment, (b) the utility loss due to data anonymization can be measured by the loss of information entropy, and (c) data anonymization can increase the utility by diversifying data sources.
